title: Connexions projectives et uniformisation : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the previous page). S is a scheme of characteristic 0 and X/S is a smooth scheme. 𝒫 = lim 𝒫_n is a complete adic O_X-algebra, augmented to O_X, with augmentation ideal J. The algebraic condition is that ω = J/J² is invertible, so 𝒫 is locally O_X[[t]] and X/S is in effect a relative curve. 𝒫 carries a connection C relative to S that respects the algebra structure but not the augmentation. One assumes the 'Kodaira–Spencer' map ω = J/J² → Ω¹_{X/S}, induced by C, is an isomorphism.

The problem. Find triples (P, σ, c) together with an isomorphism of augmented algebras u: Ŝ = O_{P̂} ≅ 𝒫 such that u(ĉ) = C. Here:
- P is a P¹-bundle ('fibré en droites', i.e. a projective line bundle) over X;
- σ is a section of P;
- c is a connection on P not preserving σ;
- P̂ is the formal completion of P along σ, and ĉ the connection induced on Ŝ.

Previously established.
- (a) An isomorphism to order 2 determines (P, σ) up to unique isomorphism.
- (b) Given (P, σ), any order-3 isomorphism u₃: Ŝ/Ĵ⁴ → 𝒫/J⁴ extending the order-2 one extends uniquely to a full formal isomorphism under which C becomes of the form ĉ.

This page. It begins with the end of (b): for c 'très régulière/transversal' in P, there is a unique u extending u₀ with u(ĉ) = C. Hence a bijective correspondence between three things:
- (a) solutions of the initial problem up to isomorphism (well defined because the category of solutions is rigid, i.e. no nontrivial automorphisms);
- (b) the canonically determined pair (P, σ) together with u₀, plus the set of order-3 extensions of u₀; this set is a pseudo-torsor under Γ(X, Ω^{⊗2}), and since Ω ≅ Ω¹_{X/S} these are relative quadratic differentials;
- (c) the set of connections c on P, transversal to σ, such that ĉ lies in a given orbit of G = Aut(P, σ) acting on Conn*(P).

The diagram summarises this: Sol ≅ Iso^!_3 (with Iso^!_0 underneath) and Sol ≅ Conn*(P)^! (connections with the uniqueness/rigidity property).

The scratch computations at the bottom are the rigidity argument for the G-action. Let g ∈ G(c), with u(C) = ĉ and g ĉ = ĉ. If gC = kĉ, then k⁻¹g C = ĉ. Then h ĉ = ĉ ⇒ h = 1, i.e. the stabiliser of ĉ is trivial, so G acts freely on transversal connections and the stabiliser computation forces g = id.

The ingredients 'Ω → Ŝ ⊗ Ω¹_{X/S}' and '∏ Ω^{⊗i} ⊗ Ω_{X/S}' prepare the next page. There the connection on Ŝ = Sym^∧(Ω) is expanded as C(ω₀) = Σ ω₀^i ⊗ ϖ_i.

In modern terms: a projective structure on a relative curve X/S is equivalent to an sl₂-oper / Gunning 'indigenous bundle' (P¹-bundle, section, connection with nondegenerate second fundamental form). Such structures are identified with formal data on the formal neighbourhood of the section. The set of these structures is an affine space (pseudo-torsor) under Γ(X, K²), and the full structure is determined by its 3-jet (the Schwarzian derivative phenomenon). This all serves the uniformization theme of the dossier.
errors: No mathematical error is visible. The torsor is correctly called a 'pseudo'-torsor, since it may be empty (e.g. no global projective structure over a general S without further hypotheses).
The final scratch lines (gC = kĉ, k⁻¹gC = ĉ, g'C = ĉ) are tentative computations, not a finished argument. The freeness of the G-action is asserted via 'hĉ = ĉ ⇒ h = 1' without written proof.

ideas.what: Projective structures on a relative curve correspond bijectively to P¹-bundles with section and transversal connection (rigid category of solutions).
ideas.usually_credited_to: Gunning (1967), Deligne (1970, Équations différentielles à points singuliers réguliers), Beilinson–Drinfeld (opers, 1990s); Mochizuki in the p-adic setting

ideas.what: Order-3 jet of the identification determines the whole formal isomorphism; extensions of an order-2 datum form a pseudo-torsor under Γ(X, Ω^{⊗2}).
ideas.modern_name: Affine space of projective structures modelled on quadratic differentials (Schwarzian derivative)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Schwarz, Poincaré); algebraic version Gunning, Deligne

ideas.what: Description via a complete adic augmented algebra with connection whose Kodaira–Spencer map J/J² → Ω¹_{X/S} is an isomorphism (formal-groupoid/crystalline viewpoint).
ideas.modern_name: Formal description of opers via jets / Harish-Chandra pairs (Aut O, formal coordinate torsor)

ideas.what: Free action of G = Aut(P,σ) on transversal connections (rigidity: h ĉ = ĉ ⇒ h = 1).
ideas.modern_name: Opers have no nontrivial automorphisms / free action of Borel gauge group

missed.claim: Grothendieck had an algebraic, relative (over arbitrary characteristic-0 base S) formulation of projective structures as formal algebras with connection, identified with P¹-bundles with transversal connection. This is essentially the oper / indigenous-bundle correspondence, with the torsor under quadratic differentials. It is an independent (undated) treatment, not a new result.
missed.quote: l'ens. des [u₃] qui prolongent u₀ — qui forment donc un pseudo torseur sous Γ(X,Ω^{⊗2})
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical: shows Grothendieck working on the algebraic theory of projective connections and uniformization in a formal-geometric, relative language anticipating opers. The mathematics itself is known.

deep.surprise_reason: The content is the standard correspondence between projective structures, opers/indigenous bundles and the affine space over quadratic differentials, here in a clean relative formal-algebra form. It is of historical interest but not new mathematics.

'l'ens. des (lg qui prolongent u₀' likely reads 'l'ens. des u₃ (isos à l'ordre 3) qui prolongent u₀'.
